Codex app-server adapter

Experimental Codex desktop adapter: additive model catalog, per-chat routing, and the index of the guides that hold its detail.

About 7 min read · 14 sections

On this page
01 Opening an unloaded subagent 02 Native picker selection 03 Codex subscription counters 04 The native relay is optional 05 Mid-turn model changes from the picker 06 Many requests for unloaded chats at once 07 Re-attaching a gateway chat 08 Native chats keep their model 09 Compaction and model changes 10 Codex 2 rows and the native catalog 11 Empty chats and message order 12 Queued messages (Cmd+Enter) 13 Processes and prediction forks on connected machines 14 Speed controls

The experimental adapter keeps the original Codex executable and native login. By default it adds configured gateway models after the native models; native picker placement is configurable in the model catalog guide. It routes every chat by its kind, not by its provider id. The adapter classifies a chat with the first rule that answers, in this order: the gateway's own provider id (gatefox, or subscription_gateway on a chat saved before 1.8.0); the registry of gateway chats; a gateway ancestor of a sub-agent, read from its saved record when this connection has not seen it; and a model alias that is not a native model slug. Any other chat is native and keeps its provider. The registry is the file <state directory>/gateway-chats/<scope>.json, where <scope> identifies the native Codex home. The adapter writes a gateway chat's start or fork to the registry before it returns the reply, a sub-agent that a gateway engine announces before it forwards the announcement, and a chat that only its ancestors or alias identified when it routes it to an executor. New gateway chats are recorded as gatefox by default (subscription_gateway before 1.8.0); a Mac whose native relay is verified can opt in to "chatIdentity": "openai" (0.4.7), so a stock engine lists them too. Existing chats keep the id they were saved with. A chat list that asks only for the native default provider also gets the gatefox and subscription_gateway chats, which is how the phone sees them through the relay. See harness identity for when to opt in, the executor contract, the phone and rollback. A gateway model alias that equals a native model slug is refused when the catalog loads, because the native slug would otherwise take over the alias's chats.

Provider usage observations are available at the authenticated GET /v1/provider-usage endpoint. Its data array holds two kinds of row. Claude rows contain only provider route IDs, recognized window/status enums, reset seconds, and observation seconds. Codex rows (kind: "codex") contain the provider route ID, the observation seconds, and a primary and/or secondary window, each with the exact usedPercent, windowMinutes and resetsAt the provider reported. Private error prose, credentials, and account identities are excluded. The daemon saves these observations privately across restart. A changed authentication-directory route (Claude), a removed provider, or a changed credential (Codex) does not inherit an old row. Clients that only know Claude rows ignore the Codex rows. The detail lives in four guides, split out of this page. Each heading below keeps its original title and anchor, and links to the page that now holds the full text.

Opening an unloaded subagent

A Multi-Agent V2 child resumes through its loaded immediate parent's SDK, on the parent's existing executor generation: starting a current-generation executor instead can return -32600 and fail hydration. thread/read and thread/turns/list still inspect saved history. Full text: Opening an unloaded subagent.

Native picker selection

nativeModelPicker lists the exact native model IDs the desktop picker offers, and nativeModelPickerPlacement (first, last, hidden) says where those rows appear. The preference belongs to the local execution host, changes no allowlist, and never rebinds a model. The page also covers the isolated native-SDK picker check. Full text: Native picker selection.

Codex subscription counters

Codex rows appear only when the Codex backend itself sends the x-codex-primary-* and x-codex-secondary-* headers or codex.rate_limits events, and a window is kept only when all three of its values are valid; a counter belongs to the credential file the request ran with. The page also covers the gateway codex-shim command, its socket rules, and gateway ssh register for the desktop SSH path. Full text: Codex subscription counters.

The native relay is optional

Nothing in the gateway depends on the native relay: an adapter or SSH listener asks once at start whether a relay is usable, and one that cannot run is left paused with its reason rather than restarted forever. This guide also holds the combined model-catalog discovery, the retired feature-key normalization and feature trimming, the refused native configuration writes, the private desktop-preferences.json, the CODEX_CLI_PATH wrapper, shared native ownership and the desktop launcher. Full text: The native relay is optional.

The login environment agent

ChatGPT is a login item and can start before the gateway sets CODEX_CLI_PATH. The unified service closes that race at its first step; standalone registration writes a managed LaunchAgent. The page covers both, the guards, rollback, API mode and what gateway desktop status reports. Full text: The login environment agent.

Mid-turn model changes from the picker

With "midTurnModelSwitch": true the adapter also offers an applied picker change to a running gateway turn, after the thread update, gated by the tokenizer recount and the SDK's own active-step check. Before it, the guide covers chat naming and Codex's active-step model switching for gateway executors. Full text: Mid-turn model changes from the picker.

Many requests for unloaded chats at once

A reconnecting app sends one request per sidebar chat. Since 1.6.5 requests for the same generation on one host connection share a single execution/acquire, and the adapter caches its "which gateway SDK" answer while the SDK's bytes are unchanged. Full text: Many requests for unloaded chats at once.

Re-attaching a gateway chat

Since 0.4.7 a gateway chat whose executor went away is loaded again on a live one before its next request, carrying only what the SDK cannot restore from the chat's own history. The page covers the once-per-chat flight, the fail-fast window, the release-skew messages and the immediate re-attach when only a shared executor socket closed. Full text: Re-attaching a gateway chat.

A listener that outlives its release

An adapter whose original package directory was pruned can continue saved chats on the managed installation's current release, but only when the marker, link, version, SDK receipt and component hashes all verify. Full text: A listener that outlives its release.

Native chats keep their model

The adapter never adds or changes model, modelProvider, config.model or config.model_reasoning_effort on a native chat's thread/resume, thread/fork, turn/start or settings update, so the signed SDK restores what the chat saved. Full text: Native chats keep their model.

Gateway sub-agents on native rows

A gateway sub-agent whose saved model is a native slug such as gpt-6.1-sol stays a gateway chat and stays on the executor that owns it; the adapter repeats its saved native model and provider only under a narrow saved-metadata check. Full text: Gateway sub-agents on native rows.

Codex 2 rows and the native catalog

Codex 2 rows borrow the harness half of the matching native row (model messages, tool mode, defaults, context-window fields and the node_repl policy) looked up by upstream_slug; everything else keeps the upstream value. The page also covers Code Mode, the recovered-SDK direct tool mode, max_context_window, executor home links and the config.toml snapshot. Full text: Codex 2 rows and the native catalog.

node_repl (browser, Chrome and computer use)

Gateway rows get the native node_repl policy, and rows with no native counterpart always require review; the codex-auto-review reviewer is served through the Codex subscription for every Auto-review approval in a gateway executor. Full text: node_repl (browser, Chrome and computer use).

Empty chats and message order

The SDK answers a thread/start or thread/fork before it announces the thread, and the desktop depends on that order, so the adapter holds a new gateway thread's notifications until the reply is written and then releases them in SDK order. Full text: Empty chats and message order.

Queued messages (Cmd+Enter)

thread/queue/* goes to the chat's own engine and the SDK owns the queue; with gateway-executor-v3 a failed gateway turn also pauses automatic dispatch, and the adapter copies local queued attachments where the service can read them. Full text: Queued messages (Cmd+Enter).
